en: Those whose intellect has transcended existence and non-existence and is without support—
they alone discern the profound meaning of conditions, which is free from objective reference. Those who do not see reality falsely imagine both saṃsāra and nirvāṇa.
Those who see reality do not conceive of either saṃsāra or nirvāṇa.
Both nirvāṇa and existence—this duality does not exist;
the supreme knowledge of existence itself is called nirvāṇa.
Whatever has arisen upon reaching this or that [condition] is, by its own nature, unarisen.
How can that which is unarisen by its own nature be called "arisen"?
At the outset, one who seeks reality should state that "everything exists."
Thereafter, for one who has realized the meaning and is free from attachment, there is solitude.
Just as the Victors have spoken of "mine" and "I" for the sake of a particular purpose,
so too have they spoken of the aggregates, the sense-bases, and the elements for the sake of a particular purpose.

The great elements and so forth, which are said to be contained within consciousness, dissolve upon the realization of that consciousness; indeed, they are falsely conceptualized. That which arises from a cause has no stability without conditions.

How can that which has ceased due to the absence of conditions be understood to exist? (NagYsk 39) When there is the acceptance of [inherent] existence, there arises the emergence of passion and hatred, the grasping of intense and corrupt views, and the disputes originating from them. (NagYsk 46)
That is the cause of all views; without it, the arising of afflictions does not occur.
Therefore, when that is fully understood, there is the complete destruction of views and afflictions. By what means is its full understanding achieved? Through the vision of dependent origination.
The best among the knowers of reality has said that what is born dependently is unborn.
... The foolish are attached to forms; those of middling capacity attain detachment;
but those of supreme intelligence, who know the intrinsic nature of form, are liberated.
